g.title: COM_QSP
g.text: Chronic Osteomyelitis · Implant-Associated Bone Infection — Quantitative Systems Pharmacology (QSP) Map
Chronic Osteomyelitis & Implant-Associated Bone Infection (Staphylococcus aureus-focused) · QSP map
The drug and the bacteria do not live in the same compartment — treatment failure arises when a
(diffusion into unperfused sequestrum: eta = tanh(phi)/phi) and a
that dose can push against, the latter an
that no dose can — this asymmetry is the entire therapeutic logic of the disease
duration only the time to reach it
— if R_ster < 1 there is no sterilisation however long the course
Bold red = the vicious circle in which the disease itself builds the pharmacokinetic barrier · bold green = therapeutic intervention · dotted = feedback/regulation · blue = measurable biomarker

g.title: cluster_inoc
g.text: Inoculum N0 and the presence of a foreign body determine everything that follows

g.title: cluster_bact
g.text: 2. Bacterial subpopulations · state transitions (the heart of the model)
The five states are not 'more or less' but
— the persister pool is a reservoir the drug never reaches

g.title: cluster_biofilm
g.text: EPS creates the diffusion delay (spatial penalty), metabolic arrest creates the Emax collapse (phenotypic penalty) — two different mechanisms

g.title: cluster_immune
g.text: Neutrophils kill bacteria but at the same time cause bone destruction and loss of perfusion — the defence is itself the cause of the barrier

g.title: cluster_bone
g.text: 5. Bone destruction · sequestrum formation — the sanctuary the disease builds for itself
Infection kills bone, and dead bone has no perfusion so the drug never arrives — the pathophysiology IS the pharmacokinetic barrier

g.title: cluster_perf
g.text: 6. Perfusion · diffusion barrier = the spatial penalty (Thiele modulus)
eta = tanh(phi)/phi, phi = L·sqrt(k_loss/D_eff) — this is a 'concentration' problem, so dose and local delivery can push against it

g.title: cluster_pk
g.text: OVIVA: where bioavailability is adequate the route (IV vs oral) does not change the outcome — what matters is the unbound bone concentration

g.title: cluster_pkbone
g.text: Plasma → vascularised bone interstitium → biofilm/sequestrum → intracellular: a multiplicative penalty at every step

g.title: cluster_pd
g.text: 9. Killing kinetics = the phenotypic penalty (Emax collapse vs EC50 shift)
KILL = C/(C+EC50) · [ Emax_gd·(mu/mu_max) + Emax_gi ] — if Emax_gi is 0, no concentration kills the persisters

g.title: cluster_abx
g.text: In osteomyelitis the axis on which a drug is chosen is not MIC but the product (bone penetration × intracellular access × non-growth killing)

g.title: cluster_surg
g.text: 11. Surgical intervention — the only means of changing the initial condition (basin)
Drugs change R_ster, surgery changes P0 and A_imp — mathematically they do not substitute for one another

g.title: cluster_tox
g.text: 12. Toxicity — efficacy that needs duration vs toxicity that duration creates
In this disease the optimal duration is the crossing point of the efficacy and toxicity curves, and debridement moves that crossing point to the left

g.title: cluster_clin
g.text: CRP (t1/2 19 h) is fast and ESR lags by weeks — they see the same event on different time axes

g.title: cluster_cov
g.text: A Cierny-Mader B host (systemic/local compromise) worsens R_ster and P0 at the same time

g.title: cluster_eq
g.text: 15. The core equations — this map compressed onto one screen

g.title: eq_1
g.text: ① Spatial penalty (dose can push against it)

g.title: pd_rster
g.text: R_ster < 1 → persistent equilibrium inside the bone (duration is meaningless)
R_ster > 1 → sterilisation possible, only time remains

g.title: eq_2
g.text: ② Phenotypic penalty (dose cannot push against it)
If Emax_gi = 0 then KILL→0 as mu→0 (independent of concentration)

g.title: pd_tster
g.text: lowering P0 is the only way to shorten T

g.title: eq_3
g.text: R_ster ≤ 1 → a stable non-zero bacterial equilibrium (duration is meaningless)

g.title: eq_4
g.text: if debridement lowers P0 by 7 log, T falls by 7·ln10/k_wake

g.title: eq_8
g.text: debridement shifts the P_cure(T) curve to the left and so shortens T*
